title: Encryption at Rest & pgcrypto
description: Protect stored data using disk volume encryption (LUKS, AWS KMS) and column-level encryption with pgcrypto.

data.text: Security compliance standards (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2) mandate encryption at rest. While storage volume encryption (AWS EBS KMS, LUKS) protects physical drives, **column-level encryption** using the **`pgcrypto`** extension protects sensitive fields (SSNs, credit card tokens) even against unauthorized database administrators.

data.title: Encrypting and Decrypting Columns with pgcrypto
data.code:
-- 1. Enable pgcrypto extension
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

-- 2. Insert encrypted data using pgp_sym_encrypt
INSERT INTO user_confidential (user_id, ssn_encrypted)
VALUES (
    'user-101',
    pgp_sym_encrypt('123-45-6789', 'secret_encryption_key', 'cipher-algo=aes256')
);

-- 3. Decrypt on retrieval
SELECT 
    user_id,
    pgp_sym_decrypt(ssn_encrypted, 'secret_encryption_key') AS ssn_decrypted
FROM user_confidential
WHERE user_id = 'user-101';

data.text: Volume encryption protects the disk, but anyone who queries the database still sees plaintext. Field-level encryption with `pgcrypto` protects the value itself, so a leaked backup or a query with broad privileges still shows ciphertext. The trade-off is that encrypted columns cannot be indexed or range-queried normally, since the same plaintext encrypts to different bytes each time.

data.title: Encrypt and decrypt a sensitive column
data.content: A random initialization vector is stored alongside the ciphertext. Decryption requires the key, which should come from a KMS or a session parameter, not a literal in the SQL.

data.title: Key management is the hard part
data.text: Encrypting the column is easy; protecting the key is the real problem. If the key lives in the same database, the same backup, or the application config, the encryption adds little. In practice the key belongs in a managed KMS and should be fetched at runtime, rotated on a schedule, and never written into SQL text or logs. Also decide deliberately whether you can accept losing the ability to index and search that column.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) or cloud volume encryption protects disk files.
Use `pgcrypto` for application-level field encryption of sensitive identifiers.
Never store encryption keys in database tables or logs.
